scope: Two separately frozen fresh-task studies. Campaign accounting includes every attempt and failure; different task corpora are not pooled for efficacy, token or latency conclusions.

policy.correctness: Every original candidate assignment succeeds with verified source/native fidelity
policy.coverage: Complete unique matched A/B/C triplets for every task and repeat; no missing or unknown cost
policy.nonregression: Focused cost per attempt and full execution time: candidate mean AND median <= each baseline overall AND in each repeat
policy.consequence: Failure or unknown evidence keeps support explicitly optional; no default promotion
policy.interpretation: Prespecified finite-corpus acceptance rule, not statistical proof or a production guarantee

reasons: Focused cost/full-time mean or median regresses or is unavailable overall or in a repeat
confirmation_promotion_gate.action: Keep support explicitly optional; do not promote defaults
confirmation_promotion_gate.control_exclusion: caller_context_supplied rows affect correctness/coverage, not benefit checks

limitations: All dollar amounts are cited standard API list-price equivalents, not actual charges or subscription savings.
Native-reported zero cache writes can reflect upstream omission; possible-write bounds are scenarios, not confidence intervals.
Original60 protected-file failures and all their attempted spend remain included; none was regraded.
Only the fresh confirmation study tests the clarified contract; its outcomes must remain separate from the initial corpus.
Workloads are small purpose-built repositories; these results do not establish production or cross-session-memory gains.
All native arms use zero configured MCP calls. Real MCP functionality passed separate installed-package checks; model efficiency through MCP is not measured.
Provider model-call counts, actual filesystem read counts and model-server resources remain unknown. Read-command and patch counts are proxies.
Local CPU is a measured lower bound; child RSS excludes parent indexing and can double-count shared pages. No local-dollar conversion is invented.
